title: “Investigation of the Benefits of Feeding Tubes (Nasogastric Feeding Tube or Gastrostomy) as an Optional Perioperative Adjunct in the Surgical Treatment of Jaw Osteonecrosis”
summary: This prospective observational study aims to investigate the impact of feeding tubes (nasogastric feeding tube or gastrostomy) on the recurrence of jaw osteonecrosis following surgical treatment of jaw osteonecrosis (AR-ONJ and IORN). Current guidelines on specific forms of jaw osteonecrosis include consensus-based recommendations regarding the use of feeding tubes. However, robust scientific evidence demonstrating their effectiveness is currently lacking. Therefore, the aim of this pilot study is to address this evidence gap, optimize the treatment regimen for jaw osteonecrosis, and establish a sound evidence base for future treatment strategies.

interventions.name: Patients with AR-ONJ or IORN receive a nasogastric feeding tube postoperatively. The primary outcome measure is wound healing (dehiscence, area of exposed bone, signs of infection, purulent discharge), which will be analyzed as a dichotomous variable (e.g., “recurrence”: yes/no).
